Leveler is one of the most important additives for super-conformal copper electroplating, which has been
widely applied in the fabrication of nanoscale (or microscale) interconnect features in integrated circuits
(ICs) and printed circuit boards (PCBs). Because the structure-property relationship of the leveler is not
clear, the development of novel leveler with high microvia filling performance is very time-consuming
and challenging. In this study, a series of triphenylmethane-based (TPM-based) molecules with different
nitrogen-containing groups have been designed, synthesized, and investigated as novel levelers for super-
conformal copper electroplating. Their structure-property relationships are investigated by electrochem-
ical analyses, contact angle measurements, and microvia filling electroplating experiments. It is found
that the steric hindrance and the type of the nitrogen-containing groups (tertiary amine or quaternary
ammonium with counter anions) in a leveler not only affect its adsorption ratio and strength on the
copper interface, but also affect its adsorption preference on different copper crystalline plane. In combi-
nation with Cl−, polyethylene glycol (PEG, suppressor), and bis-(3-sulfopropyl) disulfide (SPS, accelerator),
all TPM-based levelers show excellent microvia filling performances in copper electroplating and their ef-
fective concentrations are related to their antagonistic ability against the accelerator SPS.

crovia filling as interconnects in integrated circuits (ICs) or printed
circuit boards (PCBs) is one of the most important techniques in
modern electronic manufacturing industry [1,2]. For better stabil-
ity and reliability, the ECD copper in these nanoscale and mi-
croscale interconnect features are required to be void-free. There-
fore, a technology named “super-conformal” or “bottom-up” cop-
per electroplating has been developed and widely applied in in-
dustrial practice. The electroplating process was carried out in an
acid copper electrolyte, which was composed of copper sulfate,
sulfuric acid, chloride, and trace organic additives. Though the or-
ganic additives’ amounts in the electrolytes are very small (gener-
ally at several parts per million), the additives play a crucial role
in the super-conformal electroplating. The competitive adsorption
and differential distribution of the additives on the cathode surface
are the origination for the realization of “bottom-up” copper filling
electroplating.
According to the additives’ different electrochemical effects in
the electroplating, the additives were categorized as accelerators,
suppressors, and levelers, respectively. Bis-(3-sulfopropyl) disul-
fide (SPS) [3,4] and its reduced monomer sodium 3-mercapto-
1-propanesulfonate (MPS) [5,6] are most widely used accelera-
tors. In electroplating, the accelerators can reduce the cathodic
polarization and facilitate the copper reduction [7,8]. The sup-
pressors are usually polyether compounds, such as polyethylene
glycol (PEG) [9,10], polypropylene glycol (PPG) [11,12], or their
copolymers [13,14]. In contrast to the accelerators, the suppres-
sors synergistically work with chloride ions to increase the ca-
thodic polarization and thus suppress the copper reduction. Lev-
eler is another important additive used in the electrolyte to ful-
fill the super-conformal electroplating, which usually are nitrogen-
containing molecules and positively charged in the acid electro-
plating solution. As reported, the levelers can adsorb at the high-
density charge region of the cathode to inhibit the copper depo-
sition and level the copper surface [15]. In addition, the use of a
leveler in the microvia filling electroplating solution can greatly ex-
pand the application concentration range of accelerators [16].

Currently, most of the reported levelers are nitrogen-containing
dyes, such as the Janus Green B (JGB) [17], Alcian Blue (ABPV)
[18,19], and Diazine Black (DB)[16] etc., or non-dye hetero-
cyclic aromatic molecules, such as 2-amino-4-methylbenzothiazole
(AMBT)[20] and 2-mercaptopyridine (2-MP)[21,22] etc. Because
the structure-property relationship of the leveler is not clear
yet, the development of novel leveler with high microvia filling
performance is very time-consuming and challenging. More and
more research groups began to purposefully design and synthe-
size various nitrogen-containing levelers to study their structure-
property relationship [23–27]. In our previous study, we reported
a triphenylmethane-based leveler TPM-1, in which three pyrroli-
dine rings (nitrogen-containing functional groups) were linked by a
triphenylmethane (TPM) backbone [28]. It was found that the small
molecule with three saturated tertiary amines already be able to
show strong inhibition effect and promising microvia filling per-
formance in the copper electroplating experiments.
To further investigate the structural influence of nitrogen-
containing groups on their electrochemical properties and microvia
filling performance, a series of novel TPM-based molecules with
different nitrogen-containing functional groups were designed and
synthesized. As shown in Fig. 1, TPM-1 and TPM-3 are tertiary
amines with pyrrolidine and piperidine as the nitrogen-containing
groups, respectively. TPM-2, TPM-4, and TPM-5 are quaternary am-
moniums, in which TPM-2 and TPM-5 were methylated base on
TPM-1 with I− and Cl− as the counter anions, respectively, and
TPM-4 was methylated from TPM-3. In this study, the TPM-based
molecules were used as levelers in the super-conformal copper
electroplating and their structure-property relationship were care-
fully investigated by electrochemical analyses, contact angle mea-
surements, and microvia filling electroplating experiments.

3.3. Cyclic voltammetry measurements
To charactrized the effect of the leveler concentrations on its
electrochemical properties, cyclic voltammetry measurements with
various concentrations of TPM-based levelers (or I−) in an electro-
plating solution containing 2 ppm SPS, 40 ppm Cl− and 200 ppm
PEG have been carried out. As shown in Fig. 4, the increase of the
TPM-based levelers (or I−) concentration all leads to a further po-
larization. For TPM-1, the addition of 0.05 ppm leveler not only
decreases the absolute current density, but also changes the rel-
ative current density values in the forward (negative-going) and
backward (positive-going) sweep. As reported, the current densi-
ties in the return sweep larger than the forward values indicate
a positive feedback for the copper electroplating [38,39]. In addi-
tion, when the concentration of TPM-1 reaches as high as 8 ppm,
an evident negative differential resistance (NDR) phenomenon was
observed, which has been widely used to explain the mechanism
of extremely bottom-up filling of Cu or other metals with one sup-
pressor as the additive in electroplating [38,40–42]. Similarly, NDR
has also been observed with other TPM-based levelers at relatively
high concentrations (above 2 ppm for TPM-2 and TPM-4; above
8 for TPM-3; above 20 ppm for TPM-5). Though ternary additives
(leveler, suppressor, and accelerator) were used in this research
instead of one additive system reported in literature, extremely
bottom-up microvia filling effect has also been otained with high
concentrations of TPM-2 or TPM-4 (as shown in Figs. 7–2f, 7–2g,
7–4f, and 7–4g), which imply a gradual breakdown of the sup-
pression starting from the microvia bottom. NDR is observed for
all high concentration TPM-based levelers, however, only TPM-2
and TPM-4 result in the extremely bottom-up filling. One possi-
ble explanation is that due to the strong inhibition strength caused
by the synergistic effect of I− and the TPM-based counterpart, the
suppression layer formed by high concentration of TPM-2 (or TPM-
4) plays a predominant effect on the cathod surface and over-
shadowed the effect of SPS (as shown in Fig. 3e and f). While for
other TPM-based levelers (or I−), the antagonistic effect of SPS and
the inhibitors contributes together to achieve the super-conformal
electroplaitng, as described by the curvature enhanced adsorbate
coverage (CEAC) [36] or convection-dependent adsorption (CDA)
[43] mechanisms.

properties, and the crystalline orientations, the nitrogen-containing
groups in a leveler not only affect its adsorption strength on the

4. Conclusions
In this study, a series of novel triphenylmethane-based
molecules (TPM-2 to TPM-5) with varied nitrogen-containing func-
tional groups were synthesized and investigated as levelers for
copper super-conformal electroplating. The structure-property re-
lationships of the TPM-based levelers have been studied in detail
with electrochemical analyses, surface activity measurements, and
microvia filling electroplating experiments. It was found that all
TPM-based levelers show inhibition effect in the copper electro-
plating and their antagonistic ability against SPS followed in the
order of TPM-2 TPM-4 TPM-1 TPM-3 TPM-5. The inhibi-
tion ability of the TPM-based levelers positively correlated to their
adsorption ratio on the copper interface. Electrochemical measure-
ments demonstrate that the strongest inhibition effect of TPM-2
and TPM-4 was caused by the synergist interaction of the TPM-
based structures and the counter ion I−; the replacement of a five-
membered pyrrolidine ring (TPM-1) by a six-membered piperidine
ring (TPM-2) leads to a decrease of the leveler’s inhibition abil-
ity; the quaternization of a tertiary amine (TPM-1) with
